Constitution: Real Minorities are the Masses of this Country

Welcoming the Objectives Resolution introduced by Jawaharlal Nehru, N.G. Ranga said: Sir, there is a lot of talk about minorities. Who are the real minorities? Not the Hindus in the so-called Pakistan provinces, not the Sikhs, not even the Muslims. No, the real minorities are the masses of this country. These people are so depressed and oppressed and suppressed till now that they are not able to take advantage of the ordinary civil rights. What is the position? You go to the tribal areas. According to law, their own traditional law, their tribal law, their lands cannot be alienated. Yet our merchants go there, and in the so-called free market they are able to snatch their lands. Thus, even though the law goes against this snatching away of their lands, still the merchants are able to turn the tribal people into veritable slave by various kinds of bonds, and make them hereditary bond-slaves. Let us go to the ordinary villagers. There goes the money-lender with his money and he is able to get the villagers in his pocket. There is the landlord himself, the zamindar, and the malguzar and there are the various other people who are able to exploit these poor villagers. There is no elementary education even among these people. These are the real minorities that need protection and assurances of protection. In order to give them the necessary protection, we will need much more than this Resolution.

chapter: The Making of the Constitution (Framing the Constitution)
questionText:
Read the following excerpt carefully and answer the question that follows:

"On 13 December 1946, Jawaharlal Nehru moved the historic 'Objectives Resolution' in the Constituent Assembly: 'We are at the end of an era and possibly even the beginning of a new age... The resolution that I place before you outlines our objectives: to proclaim India as an Independent Sovereign Republic, to guarantee to all its citizens justice, social, economic and political; equality of status and opportunity; and freedom of thought, expression, belief, faith, worship, and association; and to provide adequate safeguards for minorities, backward and tribal areas, and depressed and other backward classes... We are not going to just copy what has been done in America or England; we have to fit in with the temper of our people and build a democratic socialist structure suited to the genius of India.'"

What constitutional character and status did the Objectives Resolution envision for free India?

options.text: An Independent Sovereign Republic guaranteeing fundamental democratic liberties and social justice to all citizens
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Nehru's Vision for Free India.

options.text: A theocratic Hindu state based exclusively on Manusmriti
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A permanent Dominion loyal to the British monarchy
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: An absolute military oligarchy ruled by an executive council
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for The Making of the Constitution (Framing the Constitution) (Nehru's Vision for Free India):
An Independent Sovereign Republic guaranteeing fundamental democratic liberties and social justice to all citizens

Detailed Context:
1. The Resolution proclaimed India as an Independent Sovereign Republic, affirming that all power and authority derived directly from the people.
Hence Option D is correct.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

questionText: On which historic date did the Constituent Assembly of India formally adopt, enact, and give to themselves the Constitution of India?

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for The Making of the Constitution (Framing the Constitution) (Adoption of Constitution):

Detailed Context:
1. The Constituent Assembly formally adopted and enacted the Constitution of India on 26 November 1949, when members affixed their signatures to the sacred document.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

topic: Key Figures of the Constituent Assembly
questionText:
Match the Constituent Assembly leader in List I with their historic contribution in List II:

List I:
(A) Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
(B) Jawaharlal Nehru
(C) Dr. Rajendra Prasad
(D) Sir B.N. Rau

List II:
(i) Moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946
(ii) Chairman of the Drafting Committee
(iii) Constitutional Advisor to the Assembly
(iv) Permanent President of the Constituent Assembly

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Key Figures of the Constituent Assembly.
Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for The Making of the Constitution (Framing the Constitution) (Key Figures of the Constituent Assembly):
A-ii, B-i, C-iv, D-iii

Detailed Context:
1. Ambedkar = Drafting Committee (A-ii), Nehru = Objectives Resolution (B-i), Rajendra Prasad = President (C-iv), B.N. Rau = Constitutional Advisor (D-iii).
Hence Option D is correct.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.
